## 1. Evidence boundaries and principal findings

**[CODE-VERIFIED]** The shipped worker contract separately prohibits Orca dispatch **inside a command** and **from its enclosing worker session**. These are different restrictions: WC-8 is at contract line 40; WC-13 is at line 62. Their headings are independently pinned by `RULE_PHRASES` in the worker-contract tests.

**[CODE-VERIFIED]** The worktree-agent hook does not implement either restriction. Its scanner checks whether an Orca worktree-create command has `--agent` or requests help. The ownership sentence is text printed after that scanner decides to block. Changing that sentence does not confer nested-worker authority or enforce a coordinator hierarchy.

**[CODE-VERIFIED]** The launch-level guard is an additional, independent restriction. In a governed session, non-allowlisted Orca operations become `ESCAPE`, and `ESCAPE` is denied at every governed launch level. Consequently, changing WC-13 or adding `--agent` would not, by itself, make O3 or O4 work from such a session.

**[CODE-CONTRADICTED] [STALE DOC]** The developer guide’s “Rollout state” still describes P0 and says `UNATTENDED_COMMANDS` is empty. The current test derives that set from a populated dictionary, and an uncapped heading-count search finds **31** command files with one `## Unattended mode` section each.

**[CODE-VERIFIED]** The earlier “two hook copies, two CLAUDE files, one README and two tests” claim describes only part of the current surface. The wording also exists in development and installed copies. Moreover, only one of those two tests pins the exact ownership sentence; the other pins roles and parity, not that exact phrase.

**Key Takeaways**
- Ownership wording, written worker policy and launch-level enforcement are separate change surfaces.
- No verified evidence supports treating an ownership-wording edit as an implementation of nested coordination.
- Static test pins establish shipped text and code expectations; they do not establish live Orca mailbox or depth behavior.
